questions.q: A ray of light passes from a denser medium to a rarer medium at an angle of incidence i. The reflected and refracted rays make an angle of 90° with each other. The angle of reflection and refraction are respectively r and r'. The critical angle is given by,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
r+r'+90°=180°⇒r'=90-r=90-i

n1sini=n2sinr'=n2sin(90-i)
n1sini=n2cosi⇒tani=n2n1
Now sinC=n2n1=tani
⇒C=sin-1(tani)=sin-1(tanr)

questions.q:
Consider following statements for refraction of light through prism, when angle of deviation is minimum.
(A) The refracted ray inside prism becomes parallel to the base.
(B) Larger angle prisms provide smaller angle of minimum deviation.
(C) Angle of incidence and angle of emergence becomes equal.
(D) There are always two sets of angle of incidence for which deviation will be same except at minimum deviation setting.
(E) Angle of refraction becomes double of prism angle.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\delta=\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{e}-\mathrm{A}$
For $\delta_{\text {min }} \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{e}$ and refracted ray is parallel to base $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}$ are correct

questions.q: Car <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> overtakes another car <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> at a relative speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. questions.q: An ice cube has a bubble inside. When viewed from one side the apparent distance of the bubble is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. When viewed from the opposite side, the apparent distance of the bubble is observed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the side of the ice cube is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, the refractive index of the ice cube is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's assume that the original position of the bubble is x from one side of the ice cube of side a.

When the bubble is seen from one side, it can be written that

xμ=12   ...1

For the view from the other side, it can be written that

a-xμ=4   ...2

From equations (1) and (2), it is given that

24-12μ=4μ⇒μ=2416=1.5

questions.q: A mirror is used to produce an image with magnification of $\frac{1}{4}$. If the distance between object and its image is 40 cm , then the focal length of the mirror is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=-\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}=-\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}}{-\mathrm{u}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}} \\ & \frac{1}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=4 \mathrm{v} \\ & \mathrm{v}+\mathrm{u}=40 \\ & 5 \mathrm{v}=40 \\ & \mathrm{v}=8 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \mathrm{u}=32 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}+\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{32}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{4-1}{32}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \mathrm{f}=\frac{32}{3}=10.7 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A transparent film of refractive index, 2.0 is coated on a glass slab of refractive index, 1.45. What is the minimum thickness of transparent film to be coated for the maximum transmission of Green light of wavelength 550 nm . [Assume that the light is incident nearly perpendicular to the glass surface.]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: For transmitted green light to be maxima, reflected green should be minima. $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{P}=2 \mu_0 \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n} \lambda \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{n} \lambda}{2 \mu_0} \therefore \mathrm{t}_{\min }=\frac{\lambda}{2 \mu_0}=\frac{550}{2 \times 2}=137.5 \end{aligned}$

A transparent cube of side d, made of a material of refractive index μ2, is immersed in a liquid of refractive index μ1 ( μ1<μ2). A ray is incident on the face AB at an angle θ (shown in the figure). Total internal reflection takes place at the point E on the face BC.



Then, θ must satisfy

questions.solution:
At surface (1)

μ1sinθ=μ2sinr    …1

At surface (2)

μ1=μ2sin90-r

μ1=μ2cosr ...(2)

From equation (1) and (2)

⇒sin⁡θ=sin⁡rcos⁡r

⇒sinθ=μ22-μ12μ2μ1μ2

⇒sinθ=μ22μ12-1 

θ must satisfy,

⇒θ<sin-1μ22μ12-1

questions.q: The variation of refractive index of a crown glass thin prism with wavelength of the incident light is shown. Which of the following graphs is the correct one, if $D_{m}$ is the angle of minimum deviation?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When angle of prism is small, then angle of deviation

is given by $\mathrm{D}_{\mathrm{m}}=(\mu-1) \mathrm{A}$

So, if wavelength of incident light is increased, $\mu$ decreases

and hence $\mathrm{D}_{\mathrm{m}}$ decreases.

questions.q: A biconvex lens of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> has a focal length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in air. Its focal length when immersed in a liquid of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn></math> will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, the refractive index of the material of the lens is μ1=1.5, the refractive index of the medium is μm=1.6 and the focal length of the lens in air is fa=20 cm.

In air:

1fa=μ1-12R

In liquid:

1fm=μ1μm-12R

The focal length as measured in air and that as measured inside the liquid medium are related by, 

fmfa=μ1-1μmμ1-μm   ...1

Equation (1) implies that

fm20=(1.5-1)1.6(1.5-1.6)⇒fm=-160 cm

questions.q: What is the lateral shift of a ray refracted through a parallel-sided glass slab of thickness ' $h$ ' in terms of the angle of incidence ' $i$ ' and angle of refraction ' $r$ ', if the glass slab is placed in air medium?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & A B=h \sec r \\ & B C=h \sec r \sin (\bar{i}-r) \\ & B C=\frac{h \sin (i-r)}{\cos r}\end{aligned}$

The distance at which you hold the mirror from your face in order to see your image upright with a magnification of <math><mn>5</mn></math> is

questions.solution:
m=5=-vu        ⇒v=-5u

u=45-0.4=-0.32 m
So, distance of object from mirror=0.32 m

A monochromatic light is incident at a certain angle on an equilateral triangular prism and suffers minimum deviation.

If the refractive index of the material of the prism is $\sqrt{3}$,

then the angle of incidence is :

by Snell's law $\mu_{1} \sin \mathrm{i}=\mu_{2} \sin \mathrm{r}1 \times \sin i=\sqrt{3} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow i=60$

questions.q: Consider a light ray travelling in air is incident into a medium of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msqrt></math>. The incident angle is twice that of refracting angle. Then, the angle of incidence will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let angle of incidence be θ, then angle of refraction θ2. From Snell's law, we can write,

1×sinθ=2n×sinθ2, 2sinθ2cosθ2=2nsinθ2

cosθ2=n2 ⇒θ=2cos-1n2

questions.q: A finite size object is placed normal to the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. A plane mirror is now placed in such a way that the image produced by both the mirrors coincide with each other. The distance between the two mirrors is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For Convex mirror
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{30} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{2}{30}=\frac{1}{15} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=15 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
Image formed by convex mirror is at 45 cm from object so plane mirror should be placed midway at 22.5 cm from object so that both of their images may coinside,
Therefore distance between both mirrors
$=30-22.5=7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$
Correct Answer : Option 2

questions.q: The refractive index of the material of a glass prism is $\sqrt{3}$. The angle of minimum deviation is equal to the angle of the prism. What is the angle of the prism?
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : When an object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave lens, image is formed at the centre of curvature of the lens on the other side.
Statement (II) : Concave lens always forms a virtual and erect image.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{-2 \mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{-\mathrm{f}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{-1}{2 \mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=-2 \mathrm{f} \\ & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \text { Virtual image of Real object. }\end{aligned}$
In statement II, it is not mentioned that object is real or virtual hence Statement II is false.

questions.q: In an experiment with a convex lens. The plot of the image distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></mfenced></math> against the object distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></mfenced></math> measured from the focus gives a curve <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>225</mn></math>. If all the distances are measured in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>. The magnitude of the focal length of the lens is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Newton's formula for lenses,

vu=f2 , here, f is focal length of the lens.

Given here, v'μ'=225

Thus, focal length of the lens is f2=225

Or f=15 cm

questions.q: Two convex lenses of focal length 20 cm each are placed coaxially with a separation of 60 cm between them. The image of the distant object formed by the combination is at _____ cm from the first lens.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let L1 be the first lens and L2 be the second lens.

The first refraction is in L1.

Using lens formula,

u1=∞, f1=20 cm,1v1-0=1f1 ⇒v1=20 cm

Hence, the distance between the second image and the L2 would be 60-20=40 cm.

For the second lens L2,

u2=-40 cm, f2=20 cm,1v2-1u2=1f2⇒1v2+140=120⇒1v2=140⇒v2=40 cm

So, the distance of image from first lens is

 x=40 cm+60 cm

=100 cm

questions.q: A prism of angle A=1° μ=1.5. A good estimate for the minimum angle of deviation (in degrees) is close to N10. Value of N is ………
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Angle of prism, A=1°

Refractive index of prism, μ=1.5

For this prism, minimum angle of deviation is given by

δ=(μ-1)A

⇒δ=(1.5-1)×1°=12=510=N10

⇒N=5

questions.q: Two light beams fall on a transparent material block at point 1 and 2 with angle \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_{2^{\prime}}\) respectively, as shown in figure. After refraction, the beams intersect at point 3 which is exactly on the interface at other end of the block. Given : the distance between 1 and 2, \(\mathrm{d}=4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm}\) and \(\theta_1=\theta_2=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{2 \mathrm{n}_1}\right)\), where refractive index of the block \(\mathrm{n}_2\gt\) refractive index of the outside medium \(\mathrm{n}_1\), then the thickness of the block is ________ cm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & n_1 \times \frac{n_2}{2 n_1}=n_2 \sin r \\ & \sin r=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & r=30^{\circ} \\ & \tan r=\left(\frac{d / 2}{t}\right) \\ & t=\frac{d}{2 \tan r}=\frac{d \sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{(4 \sqrt{3}) \sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & =6 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
